limited_overlap.description: 824 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 76,160 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
182 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10029 of 12000 applicants answered (83.6%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.52 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=0.0002, causal_forest=-0.0005.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -8.8; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = 0.24. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 2340 (90% -6716 to 11396).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 3946 (90% 3113 to 4780); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -3832, without months_unemployed = 3962, without education = 4125; full model = 4083.
Run time 20 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10029.
